current_answer: The commercial case is stronger: customers keep buying, and evidence now supports providers retaining some of the gain—not merely useful tools. That does not validate every capital commitment or ownership price. Strong payers can protect invoices while investment, renewal and financing absorb cash. The best-supported answer remains a real expansion with uneven, sometimes demanding return expectations—not a fictitious economy or a verdict that every AI-related share is a bubble. What the payment-and-capture evidence changes.
summary: Real paid demand. Providers can retain value. The harder question is whether enough cash reaches each investment and ownership claim.
uncertainty: Independent customers renewing at nonsubsidized prices, durable cash margins after full costs, and successful repayment and replacement across delivered investment cohorts would weaken the concern. Weak retention, greater dependence on fresh financing and poorer collateral recovery together would strengthen it—even if technical performance keeps improving.
freshness_note: Customer-dollar and renewal investigation with a 29 September retrieval boundary; underlying price, financial and earlier research observations retain their own dates.
